subject: Request: Marketplace discount variance for Skylark pilot (AWS Private Offer)
messages:
From: Jack Reynolds <jack@skylark.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SKU-level pricing for pilots (AWS private offer)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the commit options. Procurement asked me to follow up: for our proof-of-concept (3-month, ~$65k ARR equivalent), can Redwood provide a 30% off list price via AWS Private Offer? They want the discount documented in the PO so legal can align.

We can move quickly if we can land a written price and a 3-month pilot SOW.

Attaching a short SOW template we use.

Best,
Jack

Attachments: Skylark_SOW_v2.pdf
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Jack Reynolds <jack@skylark.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU-level pricing for pilots (AWS private offer)

Jack —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. I'm looping in Laura (marketplace lead) to confirm the Private Offer flow and next steps for AWS PO publish.

Quick note on pricing: we have standard pilot concessions but 30% is outside our published marketplace band for a new account at this scale. I can submit an exception request to Deal Desk with the business case (strategic logo, reference, potential expansion in Q1).

I will pull together a one-page justify and the price calc — can you confirm the expected start date and target ARR if expanded to full production? That will help the margin analysis.

Thanks,
Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Deal desk request: Skylark Inc — ask for 30% AWS Private Offer concession (DL-2026-1199)

Markus / Ben —

As discussed on the call: Skylark Inc is requesting a 30% discount on the AWS Private Offer for a 3-month pilot (~$65k commit equivalent). Business case bullets below: 
- Strategic fintech analytics customer (logos + case study ask)
- Low implementation lift: 8-week POC, potential expansion to $450k ARR within 12 months (account exec projection)
- Reference + joint webinar requested if successful

Attachments: skylark_price_calc.xlsx (I included a simple unit economic view showing LTV upside if converted).

Why we need the exception: 30% goes past standard Private Offer guidelines for first-year SMB pilots — without a concession Skylark will likely pause. They can sign quickly if we can commit to price + a short SLA carveout in the PO.

Ask: Approve 30% on a timeboxed 3-month pilot with the following guardrails:
- Max exposure: $70k total committed via AWS PO
- Roll to list pricing after the pilot unless a new commitment is signed
- Documented reference clause in SOW (marketing opt-in)

Please advise if you need more detail or if we should reduce the concession to 25% + credit.

Thanks,
Jasmine
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal desk request: Skylark Inc — ask for 30% AWS Private Offer concession (DL-2026-1199)

Jasmine —

Thanks for the write-up and the calc. A couple of clarifying Qs before I can greenlight: 
1) Is the $450k ARR projection backed by a named expansion opportunity or is this an internal forecast? We need a >50% probability to justify deeper concessions.
2) Do we have legal comfortable with the \"SLA carveout\" language you mentioned? Any redlines from Skylark legal yet?
3) Can we structure the concession as a one-time onboarding credit (applied via invoice/credit) instead of permanently reduced unit price on the marketplace listing? AWS Private Offer can accept credits in some cases, which preserves list-price integrity.

If the answers are: (1) named pipeline >50% (2) legal is OK with reference carveout (3) we can do credit, I'm inclined to approve 25% list discount + $10k onboarding credit (net economics approximates the 30% ask for the pilot but limits permanent list erosion).

Send me the named account expansion notes and any redlines and I'll escalate to finance approval if needed.

-Markus
Deal Desk / Finance Ops
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal desk request: Skylark Inc — ask for 30% AWS Private Offer concession (DL-2026-1199)

Markus —

Answers inline: 
1) Expansion projection: named opportunity in Q1 from Skylark Analytics team — they confirmed two internal use-cases and a draft scope. I'll paste exec note below. Probability per AE: ~60% contingent on POC success.
2) Legal: Skylark sent a draft SOW with standard terms; they asked us to include the pilot price in the PO. They did not send aggressive redlines (only ask: limit liability to $250k; their procurement flagged the 30% ask).
3) Credit approach: Agree — I can propose a $10k onboarding credit (applied after first invoice) + 25% list discount on the Private Offer for the 3-month term. That meets them halfway and preserves our published bands.

Attached: updated SOW (Skylark_SOW_v2.pdf) and the price calc.

If you confirm the 25% + $10k credit path, I will table that to Skylark and move to publish the Private Offer.

Thanks,
Jasmine

> Exec note from AE: Skylark Analytics leader intends to include Redwood in the Q1 ops budget; two teams (fraud detection, customer insights) already scoped 200 node-hours/month each if pilot proves accuracy at scale.
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deal desk request: Skylark Inc — ask for 30% AWS Private Offer concession (DL-2026-1199)

Jasmine / Markus —

I support the 25% + $10k onboarding credit for a timeboxed 3-month pilot with the guardrails Jasmine listed. Strategic win potential is high and sales can protect churn with a clear rollback clause. Markus — please confirm and I will sign off from GTM.

Ben
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
